record.paper_title: Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology
record.original_question: Write C_p(X) for the space of real-valued continuous functions on X with the topology of pointwise convergence, and say that spaces X and Y are t-equivalent when there exists a homeomorphism from C_p(X) onto C_p(Y). Is the unit interval I t-equivalent to the square I^2?

evidence.quote:
Below Cp(X) stands for the space of real-valued continuous functions w ith the
topology of pointwise convergence on a space X.

Following it, we say that spaces X and Y are t-equivalent

artifact.self_contained_problem: For a Tychonoff topological space $X$, let $C_p(X)$ denote the set of all continuous real-valued functions on $X$, endowed with the topology of pointwise convergence (i.e. the subspace topology inherited from the product space $\mathbb{R}^X$). Two Tychonoff spaces $X$ and $Y$ are said to be $t$-equivalent if there exists a homeomorphism between the topological spaces $C_p(X)$ and $C_p(Y)$. Let $I = [0,1]$ denote the closed unit interval, and let $I^2 = [0,1] \times [0,1]$ denote the closed unit square, both equipped with their usual Euclidean topology. Determine whether $I$ and $I^2$ are $t$-equivalent.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a long-standing problem attributed to A. V. Arhangel'skii (circa 1989), listed among selected old open problems in general topology. It is known that $I$ and $I^2$ are $l$-equivalent (linear homeomorphism of $C_p$), but whether they are $t$-equivalent (general homeomorphism of $C_p$) appears to remain unresolved in the literature surveyed. No publication establishing a resolution was found.
